definition: Saturation is the intensity or purity of a color in an image display setting. In this context, changing saturation alters how vividly tissue colors appear and can affect how easily different structures or bleeding are distinguished visually.

reasons: The packet supports saturation as a display color setting used in the NGENUITY system, but it does not explicitly support the broad dictionary gloss “the intensity or purity of a color.”

The statement that changing saturation alters how vividly tissue colors appear is not directly stated in the source; the study reports effects on contrast visibility and distinguishability of retinal hemorrhage, not a general definition of saturation.

The definition states that saturation is the “intensity or purity of a color,” but the packet only reports a specific display parameter (“saturation set to 0…or 20”) on a monitor and does not provide or support a general conceptual definition of saturation as intensity/purity.

The definition claims that changing saturation “alters how vividly tissue colors appear.” The packet does not describe tissue color vividness generally; it reports effects on measured contrast ratios and visibility of retinal hemorrhage under different monitor saturation settings.

The definition says this can affect how easily “different structures or bleeding” are distinguished visually. The packet specifically discusses distinguishing retinal hemorrhage, but it does not support a broader claim about “different structures” or “bleeding” in general.
